t:
(a) 
The Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare is authorized to develop and engage in experiments under which physicians who would otherwise be entitled to receive payment on the basis of reasonable charge, and organizations and institutions which would otherwise be entitled to reimbursement or payment on the basis of reasonable cost, for services provided—

        (1) 
under title XVIII of the Social Security Act,
 
        (2) 
under a State plan approved under title XIX of such Act, or
 
        (3) 
under a plan developed under title V of such Act,
   and which are selected by the Secretary in accordance with regulations established by the Secretary, would be reimbursed or paid in any manner mutually agreed upon by the Secretary and the physician, organization, or institution. The method of payment (in the case of physicians) or reimbursement (in the case of an organization or institution) which may be applied in such experiments shall be such as the Secretary may select and may be based on charges or costs adjusted by incentive factors and may include specific incentive payments or reductions of payments for the performance of specific actions but in any case shall be such as he determines may, through experiment, be demonstrated to have the effect of increasing the efficiency and economy of health services through the creation of additional incentives to these ends without adversely affecting the quality of such services.

    (b) 
In the case of any experiment under subsection (a), the Secretary may waive compliance with the requirements of titles XVIII, XIX, and V of the Social Security Act insofar as such requirements relate to reimbursement or payment on the basis of reasonable cost, or (in the case of physicians) on the basis of reasonable charge; and costs incurred in such experiment in excess of the costs which would otherwise be reimbursed or paid under such titles may be reimbursed or paid to the extent that such waiver applies to them (with such excess being borne by the Secretary). No experiment shall be engaged in or developed under subsection (a) until the Secretary obtains the advice and recommendations of specialists who are competent to evaluate the proposed experiment as to the soundness of its objectives, the possibilities of securing productive results, the adequacy of resources to conduct the proposed experiment, and its relationship to other similar experiments already completed or in process.
 
    (c) 
Section 1875(b) of the Social Security Act is amended by inserting after “under parts A and B” the following: “(including the experimentation authorized by section 402 of the Social Security Amendments of 1967)”.

fable.w: Before deciding to develop or engage in a payment experiment, the Secretary must obtain the advice and recommendations of expert specialists, which is expert consultation ahead of a federal decision. The section also has participants selected "in accordance with regulations established by the Secretary," and rulemaking authority counts as participation. The tempting contrary reading is that the specialists could be federal employees or that this is merely about provider payment arrangements, but the text sets up an expert-review gate on the Secretary's decision, which is most naturally read as drawing on experts outside the government.
fable.s: No experiment shall be engaged in or developed under subsection (a) until the Secretary obtains the advice and recommendations of specialists who are competent to evaluate the proposed experiment

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to obtain advice and recommendations from 'specialists' before engaging in experiments. These specialists are outside the federal government (as they are not defined as federal employees or agencies), and their input is a prerequisite for the federal decision to proceed with the experiment. This constitutes participation by outside experts in a federal decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: No experiment shall be engaged in or developed under subsection (a) until the Secretary obtains the advice and recommendations of specialists who are competent to evaluate the proposed experiment as to the soundness of its objectives, the possibilities of securing productive results, the adequacy of resources to conduct the proposed experiment, and its relationship to other similar experiments already completed or in process.

opus.w: Before the Secretary decides to engage in or develop an experiment, he must get advice and recommendations from competent specialists, which is expert consultation built into a federal decision. Separately, the section requires the Secretary to select participants under regulations, which counts as rulemaking. The tempting 'No' reading treats the specialists as possibly federal staff or the payment terms as mere contracting. But the definition names expert consultation and rulemaking as participation, and this advice is a precondition for a federal decision, not just input to a report.
opus.s: No experiment shall be engaged in or developed under subsection (a) until the Secretary obtains the advice and recommendations of specialists who are competent to evaluate the proposed experiment as to the soundness of its objectives
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The specialists could be federal employees, and "mutually agreed upon" payment terms look like contract negotiation, which is not participation. That reading fails here. The Secretary cannot start or develop any experiment until he "obtains the advice and recommendations of specialists," which is a required outside-expert review before a federal decision. The section also requires the Secretary to choose participants "in accordance with regulations established by the Secretary," which counts as rulemaking under the definition. This is unlike the study in Example 3, because the advice here comes before a federal decision about whether to go ahead with an experiment.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires that the method of reimbursement or payment be 'mutually agreed upon' by the Secretary and the private physicians, organizations, or institutions. This necessitates consultation and coordination with non-federal parties (outside the government) before the federal decision on payment terms is finalized. While the mention of 'specialists' is ambiguous regarding their employment status, the mutual agreement with private providers clearly involves outside parties in the decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: would be reimbursed or paid in any manner mutually agreed upon by the Secretary and the physician, organization, or institution.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "specialists" are outside experts and thus their advice constitutes participation. However, the text does not specify that these specialists are independent of the federal government; they could be federal employees. More importantly, the core mechanism described in subsection (a) is a "mutual agreement" between the Secretary and private parties (physicians, organizations, institutions) regarding payment terms. This negotiation and agreement process involves non-federal parties in the decision-making regarding how they are reimbursed, which fits the definition of participation (consultation/coordination with people outside the government). The "mutually agreed upon" language is the strongest indicator of participation here, as it requires the federal government to coordinate with and obtain agreement from outside entities before implementing the payment method.
